User Task

General Concept: A User Task in BPMN is used to represent work that must be performed by a human user. It is typically used for approvals, data entry, or other manual activities in a process.

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, a User Task creates a task for a user or group, which can be claimed, completed, or delegated. Input and output mappings are defined using FEEL expressions. User Tasks support assignment rules, deadlines, and escalation. Variable scoping ensures only mapped variables are visible to the user. The engine integrates with the TaktX client for user interaction and task management.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
A User Task in TaktX allows you to:

  • Configure input and output mappings using FEEL expressions for flexible data transformation.
  • Assign tasks to users or groups for manual processing.
  • Set up deadlines, reminders, and escalation for timely completion.
  • Integrate with user interfaces or task lists for human interaction.
  • Monitor execution and audit results via the TaktX client.
  • Attach boundary events for error, escalation, or timer handling.

 

Example: Leave Request Process with User Task

 

This example shows a process where an employee submits a leave request, a User Task is used for manager approval, and the process continues to notification. The User Task demonstrates human interaction and approval workflows.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use assignment rules to direct tasks to the right users or groups.
  • Configure deadlines and escalation for timely completion.
  • Limit variable scope to only what the user needs.
  • Document task instructions and expected outcomes.

Pitfalls:

  • Unassigned tasks may block process progress.
  • Unmapped variables will not be visible to the user.
  • Incomplete tasks can delay process completion.
